definitions.explanation: A thick string made by twisting fibers together, traditionally made from straw or hemp in Japan.

examples.japanese: {荷物|にもつ}を{縄|なわ}でしっかり{縛|しば}った。
examples.english: I tied the luggage tightly with rope.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{縄|なわ}{跳|と}びをしている。
{犯人|はんにん}は{縄|なわ}で{縛|しば}られた。
examples.english: The criminal was tied up with rope.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{縄|なわ}はすぐ{切|き}れるから、{新|あたら}しいのを{使|つか}おう。
examples.english: Old rope breaks easily, so let's use new one.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りの{前|まえ}に、{村|むら}の{人|ひと}たちが{力|ちから}を{合|あ}わせて{太|ふと}い{縄|なわ}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: Before the festival, the villagers worked together to make a thick rope.

notes:
USAGE: {縄|なわ} traditionally refers to rope made from natural fibers like straw ({藁|わら}) or hemp ({麻|あさ}). It's used in various contexts from practical binding to cultural practices.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{縄|なわ}{跳|と}び (jump rope)
・{縄|なわ}{張|ば}り (territory, turf)
・{縄|なわ}を{解|と}く (to untie rope)
・{縄|なわ}で{縛|しば}る (to tie with rope)

CULTURAL NOTES:
・{注連縄|しめなわ} (shimenawa) - sacred rope used at Shinto shrines
・{縄文|じょうもん}{時代|じだい} (Jomon period) - named after rope-patterned pottery

SIMILAR WORDS:
・ロープ - rope (loanword, general)
・{紐|ひも} - string, cord (thinner)
・{綱|つな} - thick rope, hawser
